trust_decision.summary: A token request is re-signed for whatever origin the response Location header names, so the decision is: do not follow a token-endpoint redirect to a different scheme/host/port unless the caller opted in; decided in OAuth::Consumer#token_request's 3xx branch, which resolves the Location against the current token-request URI and compares origins before recursing.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary is about token-request redirects; the only code in the tree that reads a Location header and re-issues a signed token request is the 300..399 branch of Consumer#token_request.

fix_sites.module_kind: public API constructor / class-level default options (lib/oauth/consumer.rb:51-93, merged at lib/oauth/consumer.rb:127-128)

fix_sites.entry_point: internal helpers reached only via #token_request (token_request_options, token_request_uri, token_request_redirect_uri, token_request_redirect_path, max/cross-origin accessors, effective port)
fix_sites.module_kind: new internal helpers (URI resolution and origin comparison)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: RequestToken#get_access_token only delegates to consumer.token_request, so a fix inside Consumer#token_request already covers it and no separate site needs hardening.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Same-origin (absolute and relative) token-endpoint redirects must still be followed, the response block form must still yield the body after a redirect, and consumer.site/consumer.http must stay pointed at the configured provider so the later access-token exchange still works; a fix that errors on every 3xx or that keeps rewriting options[:site] breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: relative Location resolved against the current token-request path
absolute cross-origin Location (rejected unless opted in)
origin compared on scheme, host and port with default-port normalisation (443/80)
redirect chains bounded by a maximum (default 10, per-call override)
token_request path passed as an absolute URL versus a relative path (token_request_uri absolute? branch)
per-request option values overriding the consumer-level defaults

O8b_injection_room.sibling: redirect following for authenticated service calls (AccessToken#request already re-points the consumer at an absolute URI and restores it in ensure)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: many providers answer POSTs with a 302 to a canonical service URL, so a maintainer would plausibly add the same origin policy here

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a shared redirect policy on the lower-level #request primitive when the path is an absolute URL
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the token handler's absolute-path case is delegated to this branch, so moving the policy down one layer is a natural refactor

O8b_injection_room.sibling: redirect policy carried through marshal_dump/marshal_load of the consumer's options
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: consumers are commonly stashed in the session, and options are already dumped wholesale

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second transport's oauth! path with its own redirect handling
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the gem ships two client adapters, so a maintainer adding redirect support per transport is credible

O9_family: Origin validation error leading to credential/metadata exposure on redirect (CWE-346 with CWE-200 and SSRF-adjacent CWE-918): a signed OAuth token request is re-signed for a redirect-named origin

O10_build.toolchain: bundler + RSpec via Rakefile; .rspec and spec/spec_helper.rb; Gemfile pulls modular gemfiles and a local ../nomono path unless RUBY_OAUTH_DEV=false
O10_build.project_tests: spec/oauth/consumer_spec.rb, spec/oauth/consumer_integration_spec.rb, spec/oauth/request_token_spec.rb, spec/oauth/access_token_spec.rb; WebMock and VCR (oauth.gemspec:179-180) stub all HTTP, so the area runs offline; at the pinned commit there are no redirect tests at all (no spec mentions 'redirect' or 'token_request')

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Compare the Location host with the site host and raise on mismatch, leaving the rest of the 3xx branch (path-only comparison, options[:site] rewrite, no redirect bound, no block/argument forwarding) as it is.

out_of_scope_notes: In the fixed revision the opt-in cross-origin path still lets the lower-level #request re-target the consumer's memoised @http to the other origin (lib/oauth/consumer.rb:254-259 with the @uri memo at lib/oauth/consumer.rb:152-159); this is outside the pinned-commit screening and was not pursued.
